title: Keep TLS certificate verification on
when: Code calling HTTPS services turns certificate checks off (rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, verify=False) or hits certificate errors, and needs a fix that keeps checks on.
prompt:
Goal: All outbound TLS checks the chain and hostname; private or self signed endpoints are trusted by adding their CA, never by turning checks off.
Steps:
1. Search code, config, scripts and CI for rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, checkServerIdentity overrides, verify=False, ssl._create_unverified_context, CERT_NONE and curl -k.
2. Find why each was added: self signed dev server, intercepting proxy, internal CA, expired certificate, wrong hostname.
3. Internal CA: pass ca: readFileSync("certs/internal-ca.pem") to an https.Agent or set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS; in Python verify="certs/internal-ca.pem".
4. Local development: a local CA and localhost certificate trusted on the dev machine only; never ship a disabling flag.
5. Hostname mismatch or expiry: fix the certificate on the server; do not override checkServerIdentity.
6. Startup guard: exit with an error when NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED is "0" in production.
Quality bar:
- Shipped code has zero disabled checks.
- CA files are public certificates only.
- TLS 1.2 minimum where you configure clients or servers.
Pitfalls:
- A "just this call" bypass that later becomes the shared client.
- Committing the CA private key next to the certificate.
- Pinning a leaf certificate that expires and breaks the app.
Verify:
- [ ] The search finds no disabled checks.
- [ ] Private endpoints work with an explicit CA.
- [ ] The production guard exists.
- [ ] No private key files are in the repo.
Output: Fixed client code, certs/README.md about the CA, findings in SECURITY-AUDIT.md.

examples.input: coloquei rejectUnauthorized false porque o servidor interno usa certificado proprio
examples.output: ca option with internal-ca.pem, bypass removed, production guard for NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED
